key_insight: The paper introduces iPANNs and fPANNs to learn physics-consistent lower, mean, and upper hyperelastic constitutive responses that bound noisy stress data and represent uncertainty explicitly.
engineering_relevance: This provides a compact, distribution-free way to quantify and propagate aleatoric uncertainty in constitutive laws for more reliable mechanics and finite element simulations.
method: Learn sparse free-energy density branches with a physics-augmented neural network and obtain stress via automatic differentiation.
Use a two-stage transfer-learning process: fit a sparse mean model first, then fine-tune lower and upper bound branches.
Embed iPANN bounds into a fuzzy-set formulation via alpha-cut interpolation to produce nested admissible responses.
evidence_signal: The models were tested on synthetic isotropic hyperelastic data with heteroscedastic noise, random realizations, shifted noise means, and varying noise magnitudes, and the learned bounds enclosed noisy stress observations while generalizing to the test set.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the assumed physics constraints and the two-stage training setup, so overly sparse or misspecified energy forms may limit robustness.
paper_title: Interval and fuzzy physics-augmented neural networks (iPANN and fPANN) for uncertainty quantification and propagation in constitutive modeling
